title: Statistical Mechanics of Non-Abelian Learnability Transitions
abstract: Monitored many-body quantum systems can undergo sharp learnability transitions characterized by how much information can be learned by the observer. When the dynamics conserves a non-Abelian charge, such as an $SU(2)$ spin, understanding how the observer learns the total charge remains an outstanding problem. Unlike the Abelian case, where charge measurements on distinct sites commute, the $SU(2)$-symmetric readouts are noncommuting fusion measurements, making learning a genuinely quantum inference problem. In this work, we propose a theory of $1+1d$ monitored quantum dynamics with $SU(2)$ symmetry, and show that it can be described by an effective replicated loop model comprised of a replica-pairing field and a diffusive ($z=2$) background sector that carries the $SU(2)$ charge and remains gapless throughout the phase diagram. Our theory predicts that the "spin-sharpening'' and entanglement transitions coincide as a single transition. Ordering of the pairing field produces volume-law entanglement and hides the background sector from measurements, leading to a learning time of $t\sim L^{3}$ for the total spin. When the pairing field disorders, the background sector alone gives logarithmic entanglement and a diffusive learning time $t\sim L^{2}$. Our analysis is controlled by a large-loop-fugacity expansion.
summary: This work develops a statistical mechanics theory for monitoring quantum systems with non-Abelian symmetries, treating information acquisition as a quantum inference problem. By mapping the dynamics to a loop model, the authors predict that the system exhibits distinct learning time behaviors—$L^3$ versus $L^2$—depending on the phase transition of the underlying pairing field. This provides a powerful framework for understanding how measurement constraints govern quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how much information an observer can learn about a many-body quantum system whose dynamics conserves a non-Abelian charge, framing it as a quantum inference problem.
main_result: The theory predicts that the 'spin-sharpening' and entanglement transitions coincide, yielding distinct learning time scalings ($t \sim L^3$ vs $t \sim L^2$) depending on whether the pairing field is ordered or disordered.
method: The analysis employs the replica trick and a large-loop-fugacity expansion to map the monitored quantum dynamics onto an effective replicated loop model.
model_or_system: The system is a 1+1 dimensional monitored quantum system with SU(2) symmetry, modeled by a circuit evolving via unitary gates and projective measurements. The dynamics are analyzed via an effective replicated loop model with two coupled sectors.

important_parameters: System size ($L$), measurement probability ($p$), and the replica structure ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the replica trick and the large-loop-fugacity expansion, treating the background sector as a diffusive ($z=2$) critical sector.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by mapping the dynamics to a loop model, analyzing the effective interactions in the pairing sector, and deriving the scaling laws for entanglement and learning time in the distinct ordered and disordered phases.
why_interesting: It connects concepts from quantum information theory (learnability) directly to critical phenomena and phase transitions in condensed matter systems, providing quantitative predictions for time scales based on symmetry breaking.
